name: Prune Activity (registry-quality)
description: Sibling #3 of the registry-quality-pass per OpenSpec change 2026-04-27-activity-registry-quality-pass. Consumes activityReview[] (from review-activity) and dispatches `activityTemplate_deprecate` write resolver calls for templates with severity >= minSeverity (default 4) that are NOT in coreActivitySet. Three tasks: (1) filter_deprecation_candidates — iteration over reviews; condition: severity >= minSeverity AND NOT in coreActivitySet; aggregateAs=list; emits pruneCandidate[]; (2) dispatch_deprecate_impulses — iteration over pruneCandidates; body=impulse-resolve with pointer.type=`activityTemplate_deprecate` (write resolver); aggregateAs=list. GATE on admin scope (the deprecate handler is admin-only via SurrealDB PERMISSIONS); 401 responses are expected when the calling identity lacks admin scope. dryRun=true (default) skips this task entirely; emit_prune_report still runs and surfaces the pruneCandidates as an audit signal; (3) emit_prune_report — llm summarizes the deprecation attempts (success vs 401-blocked vs dry-run-skipped); emits auditReport + goalEnd. CONTEXT-BUDGET: per-template deprecate dispatch carries only the templateId in the pointer; no template bodies echoed. dryRun guard makes the chain observable-without-mutation by default.

variables.name: minSeverity
variables.description: Minimum activityReview.severity for prune eligibility. Default 4 matches review-activity's score_severity scale: 4=serious (any 'fail' on idiom_alignment OR sandbox_hygiene), 5=should-deprecate. Lower (e.g. 3) is more aggressive; higher (5) is conservative-only-deprecate-the-worst. The filter_deprecation_candidates iteration body uses the elementVar's severity field to match; reviews with severity below the threshold are dropped from the candidate list.

variables.name: dryRun
variables.description: When true (the default), filter_deprecation_candidates emits the pruneCandidate list but dispatch_deprecate_impulses is skipped via conditional. emit_prune_report still runs and surfaces the dry-run candidates as an audit signal. Flip to false to actually issue activityTemplate_deprecate write calls — gated on admin scope (the deprecate handler is admin-only via SurrealDB PERMISSIONS); when the calling identity lacks admin scope, the write resolver returns 401/403 and the chain still completes with a structured failure report. RECOMMENDED: keep dryRun=true on first invocations; flip only after auditReport from the dry run shows expected candidate set.

tasks.description: Iterate over the activityReview[] from the impulse pool (scored_reviews, emitted by review-activity's score_severity task).

config.prompt:
You are filtering an activity review for prune eligibility.

REVIEW:
{{review}}

CORE ACTIVITY SET (do NOT prune these — they are the load-bearing core):
{{impulse:targets_list}}

GATES:
1. review.severity >= {{minSeverity}}
2. review.templateId NOT IN coreActivitySet

If BOTH gates pass, output a pruneCandidate. Otherwise output null.

Output EXACTLY this JSON (no markdown, no prose):
If eligible:
{"templateId":"<review.templateId>","severity":<number>,"reason":"<one-line summary derived from review.findings + severityRationale>","summary":"<copy review.summary>"}

If not eligible:
null

tasks.notes: For each review, the iteration body LLM checks: severity >= {{minSeverity}} AND templateId NOT IN coreActivitySet (read from impulse:targets_list — the coreActivitySet slice carried over from review-activity, OR coreActivitySet directly when both activities run in the same session). Reviews failing either guard are filtered out. The remaining set is emitted as pruneCandidate impulses with reason: severity, findings summary. SIMPLIFICATION: the filter is implemented in an LLM body for first ship — a deterministic `severity_filter` resolver is the proper fix once the heuristic stabilizes (post-ship ribosome extraction). When activityReview[] is empty (review-activity not run OR no candidates), the iteration emits zero pruneCandidates and the chain still terminates cleanly with an empty pruneCandidate list.

tasks.description: Iterate over the pruneCandidates from filter_deprecation_candidates and dispatch `activityTemplate_deprecate` write resolver calls per candidate.
tasks.notes: Each per-iteration body calls impulse-resolve with pointer.type=activityTemplate_deprecate, target_id=candidate.templateId, reason=candidate.reason. ADMIN-SCOPE GATE: the deprecate handler is admin-only via SurrealDB PERMISSIONS (per docs/impulse-types/LEARNING_LOOP_WRITE_RESOLVERS.md). When the calling identity lacks admin scope, the resolver returns 401/403 and aggregateAs=list captures the per-iteration error. Conditional gate: dryRun != true — when dryRun=true (the default), this task is skipped entirely. SIMPLIFICATION: the spec's intended idiom is a per-task scope check before dispatch (with a single 401 short-circuiting the whole iteration); we let each iteration's resolver call surface its own scope error so the audit signal is per-template (which template actually got deprecated, which 401-blocked). When iteration is NOT registered (sibling work), this task fails with `resolver not found` and the trace records the failure_mode for ribosome.

tasks.description: LLM summarizes the prune attempt and emits an auditReport + goalEnd matching make-activity's emission contract at make-activity.json:declare_complete.

config.prompt:
You are emitting the final prune report for a prune-activity invocation.

INPUTS:
- PRUNE CANDIDATES (from filter_deprecation_candidates): {{impulse:prune_candidates}}
- DEPRECATE RESULTS (from dispatch_deprecate_impulses; null when dryRun=true): {{impulse:deprecate_results}}
- DRY RUN FLAG: {{variables.dryRun}}
- MIN SEVERITY: {{variables.minSeverity}}

Produce a structured audit report with these sections:
1. total_candidates — count of pruneCandidates
2. dispatched_count — count of deprecate dispatch attempts (0 when dryRun=true)
3. success_count — deprecate_results entries with no `error` field
4. error_count — deprecate_results entries with `error` (typically 401/403 from admin-scope gate)
5. dry_run_flag — copy from variables.dryRun
6. candidates — array of {templateId, severity, reason, summary} (all pruneCandidates)
7. errors — array of {templateId, error_message, status_code} for any error_count entries
8. forward_pointers — replace-activity (severity 2-3, not touched here); extract-pattern (longer-horizon)

Then call markGoalComplete with:
- summary: 2-3 sentence description (e.g. 'identified N prune candidates at minSeverity={{variables.minSeverity}}; dryRun=true so no deprecate calls dispatched' OR 'dispatched M deprecate calls; K succeeded, L failed with 401 (admin scope required)')
- achievedShapes: ['pruneCandidate', 'auditReport'] (and 'activityTemplate_deprecate_result' when dryRun=false)
- evidence: array of {kind: 'impulse', ref: <impulse-id>, observation}

Output EXACTLY this JSON (no markdown, no prose):
{"text":"<summary>","achievedShapes":["pruneCandidate","auditReport"],"evidence":[<rows>],"goalSucceeded":<true|false>,"completedAt":"<ISO-8601>","auditReport":{"total_candidates":<n>,"dispatched_count":<n>,"success_count":<n>,"error_count":<n>,"dry_run_flag":<bool>,"candidates":[...],"errors":[...],"forward_pointers":[...]}}

No other fields. No commentary.
config._tool_note: Same prompt-enforced markGoalComplete contract as make-activity.json:declare_complete and core-activity-audit.json:emit_audit_report.

tasks.notes: The auditReport carries: total_candidates (count of pruneCandidates from filter_deprecation_candidates), dispatched_count (count of dispatch attempts; 0 when dryRun=true), success_count (deprecate_results with no error field), error_count (deprecate_results with error — typically 401/403 when calling identity lacks admin scope), dry_run_flag, candidates (the full pruneCandidate list, each with severity + reason). When dryRun=true the report's success_count and error_count are 0 and the candidates section is the actionable signal; when dryRun=false the report stratifies success vs error and the operator can read the audit trail. forward_pointers: replace-activity for severity 2-3 reviews (which prune-activity does not touch); extract-pattern for traces from successfully-deprecated templates (longer-horizon).

metadata.author: activity-registry-quality-pass

preexisting: activityTemplate_deprecate (write resolver, advertised by activity-api per docs/impulse-types/LEARNING_LOOP_WRITE_RESOLVERS.md)
activityTemplate_deprecate_result (response shape from the write resolver)
newOrInformal: pruneCandidate — filtered subset of activityReview[] eligible for deprecation; carries {templateId, severity, reason, summary}

openQuestions: DEFAULT-DRY-RUN POSTURE: dryRun defaults to true so first invocations are observable-without-mutation. The trade-off is that operators must explicitly flip the flag to actually deprecate; this is intentional given that activityTemplate_deprecate is admin-gated and irreversible-in-effect (the deprecated tag is set; subsequent invocations of that template are blocked). FOLLOW-UP: when the audit pipeline matures (after enough auditReports show predictable candidate sets), consider flipping the default to false in the boredom-task variant of this activity.

401/403 HANDLING: when the calling identity lacks admin scope, each per-iteration impulse-resolve call to activityTemplate_deprecate returns 401 or 403. The iteration aggregateAs=list captures these as per-iteration errors, so the audit signal is per-template (which templates got deprecated, which were blocked). SIMPLIFICATION: the chain does not short-circuit on the first 401 — it tries each candidate and reports the full success/error split. Operators reading the auditReport see whether a scope misconfiguration is the issue (all errors) vs a partial-permission case (some errors, some successes). FOLLOW-UP: add a precursor scope-check task that calls a hypothetical `identity.has_scope` resolver and short-circuits the chain when the scope is missing.

FILTER-IN-LLM: filter_deprecation_candidates uses an LLM iteration body to apply the severity + coreActivitySet exclusion gates. This is per-review LLM cost when a deterministic filter would suffice. SIMPLIFICATION: today the LLM body is bounded at maxTokens=250 per iteration; total cost for typical N=10 reviews is ~2.5K output tokens. FOLLOW-UP: register a deterministic `severity_filter` resolver that consumes the activityReview list + minSeverity + coreActivitySet and emits the pruneCandidate list without an LLM call (post-ship ribosome extraction).

REASON STRING ESCAPING: the iteration body's pointer config interpolates {{candidate.reason}} into the activityTemplate_deprecate pointer. When candidate.reason contains JSON-special characters (quotes, backslashes), the impulse-resolve call may produce malformed JSON. SIMPLIFICATION: the LLM body in filter_deprecation_candidates is instructed to emit reason as a one-line string (no quotes, no newlines); the JSON-stringification at iteration-resolve time handles escaping. FOLLOW-UP: add explicit escaping in the iteration resolver's interpolation path, OR enforce a max-length + alphanumeric+space-only constraint on reason.
limitations: WRITE-GATED — gated on admin scope (activityTemplate_deprecate is admin-only). Default dryRun=true makes the chain observable-without-mutation; flip to false only after an audit run shows the expected candidate set.

Severity filter is heuristic — relies on review-activity's severity scoring (which is itself heuristic). Treat the prune candidate list as informative-not-canonical; an operator review step is recommended before flipping dryRun=false.
When activityReview[] is empty (review-activity not run in current session), the chain emits a goalEnd impulse describing the no-op (zero candidates).

401/403 errors do not short-circuit the iteration — each candidate is attempted and reported separately. The auditReport stratifies success vs error so an operator can diagnose scope misconfiguration vs partial permissions.
metadata.outputContract: Always emits an `auditReport` impulse via emit_prune_report plus a `goalEnd` for explicit completion. When dryRun=false AND any deprecate call succeeds, also emits per-iteration `activityTemplate_deprecate_result` impulses (aggregated in deprecate_results).
metadata.subscriberContract: Not a lifecycle subscriber. Dispatched explicitly — typically after review-activity completes and the operator (or a registry-quality orchestrator) decides to escalate to deprecation.
metadata.spec_reference: OpenSpec change 2026-04-27-activity-registry-quality-pass (sibling #3 of 6). Sibling spec to 2026-04-27-meta-activity-builder.
